summary:
The core is sound and I checked it against the tree. FolderDone is the only place that stamps Unreadable or adds to _unreadable (Scanner.cs:397-398; nothing else in src does). SetChildren runs before the stamp. The root's call passes opened:true. EntryClassifier makes name-surrogate reparse points Links before Folders. The two new rules already sit under '# settled by SL-005', so they need no xUnit twin, and today's tree matches neither. The note wording passes the existing fixed-plural, kind-words and not-read-yet rules. The cited rustfs PR #8479 says what the design claims. The repro asserts only Unreadable.Count==0 and the flag, so the design makes it pass.

Two majors:
- The precondition the design marked must-verify (2/3 means the folder is gone) fails in a way it did not consider: it cannot tell a deleted folder from a lost drive letter or a disconnected mapped share. For those, every queued folder's open fails with 3. The design would turn honest 'could not be opened' rows into 'deleted, counted as an empty folder' and remove the 'may be missing' captions. The letter-loss case can be measured here with a SUBST letter TAAD creates, yet the design filed only SMB/DFS/ReFS, for a person.
- Material cases 2, 3, 10 and 11 check only against E007* tests that do not exist anywhere in the tree. Lessons #876, #888 and #896 record the same absence three times.

One minor: the two new text rules miss the most likely second spelling, including the spike's own patch.

findings.claim:
FolderVanished = !opened && SizeProbe.IsGone(error) counts a folder as deleted whenever its open fails with 2 or 3. It cannot tell 'this folder was deleted' from 'the path above it stopped resolving':
- a drive letter removed mid-scan (USB stick pulled, a SUBST or `net use /d` removed), where \\?\Q:\child no longer resolves;
- a mapped share that dropped. Axcient's KB lists error 3 with 'If this is a network mapped drive, then it has been disconnected' (https://help.axcient.com/en_US/115002869807-BACKUP-FOR-FILES-Troubleshoot-Backup-for-Files/115010655808-Backup-for-Files-Backup-fails-due-to-path-not-found-error), and an Unavailable mapped drive answers 'The system cannot find the path specified' (https://stackoverflow.com/questions/1703304).

In either case every folder still on _pending fails with 3. The design counts each one in FoldersVanished and keeps it as an empty folder, so Unreadable drops to 0. The Unreadable tab hides, the 'may be missing' captions go, and the scan ends Completed with the rest of the drive silently missing and a note claiming the folders were deleted. Today the same folders are honest 'could not be opened' rows.

This is the transfer's must-verify invariant failing. It also bears on the next proof run: W-003 cuts a mapped share mid-scan, and Get-ShareVerdict never reads the notes, so a 'held' record could ship that false ending. The design filed only SMB/DFS/ReFS/FAT for a person. The letter-loss half can be measured on this PC with a SUBST letter TAAD itself creates.
findings.class_of: gone codes caused by losing the volume, drive letter or share above the folder, not the folder itself

quote.text: public static bool IsGone(int error) => error is Kernel32.ERROR_FILE_NOT_FOUND or Kernel32.ERROR_PATH_NOT_FOUND;

findings.evidence: Design component 'Scanner.FolderVanished' and cross_domain_transfer invariant '2 and 3 mean gone on SMB shares, DFS links ...' (status must-verify). Outside claim 8, recalled. Scanner.cs:394-398 is the only stamp. Measurement not yet made: SUBST a scratch tree as a free letter, scan the letter with ScanOptions.AfterFolder, and at n==1 remove the letter (DefineDosDevice with DDD_REMOVE_DEFINITION, which TAAD owns). Then read the pending folders' Win32Error. Expected 3.
findings.fix: Measure first with the SUBST probe above. Then, in FolderDone's gone branch only, check that the scan root still opens: one io.Open of win32Root with keepLastAccess false, cancellable like every other open. If it does not open, stamp the folder unreadable as today. Add a VanishedFolderTests case on a SUBST letter removed mid-scan: Unreadable keeps the queued folders and FoldersVanished is 0.

findings.evidence: Glob tests/**/E007* gives no files. Grep 'E007' over the repository gives only .taad/slices/SL-005/design-slice-1.json. The design's case checks name FullyQualifiedName~FsAnalyser.Core.Tests.E007*Tests with RunConfiguration.TreatNoTestsAsError=true.
findings.fix:
Have the builder own the material checks:
- In VanishedFolderTests, assert row y's UnreadableBelow is 0 and w carries no flag in the code-3 case, and add the control: a TempTree.Deny folder stays in Unreadable as 5/NothingListed beside a deleted one.
- For the App side, add a tests/window/SL-005-*.Tests.ps1 report-mode case (listed as a non-launcher in tests/window/AppArgumentCorpus.json, per #876). It checks OutcomeNotes.lines, the two captions, the tab, core.unreadable and core.foldersVanished.
- Alternatively, point cases 2, 3, 10 and 11 only at tests that exist when build starts.

findings.claim:
Each of the two new text rules misses the most likely second spelling of what it forbids.
- Scanner.cs forbids only the constant names. `error == 2 || error == 3`, which is literally the spike folderdone-open-2-3-as-gone's patch, passes the rule and drifts from SizeProbe.IsGone exactly as the rule's 'because' fears. The FolderVanished theory only pins today's codes, so it cannot catch that drift.
- DirectoryReader.cs forbids IsGone( and ERROR_PATH_NOT_FOUND but not ERROR_FILE_NOT_FOUND, because List already uses that constant at line 152. So `if (error == Kernel32.ERROR_FILE_NOT_FOUND) return 0;` after Open swallows the main gone code (2) and passes. VanishedFolderTests' FoldersVanished==1 assertion would catch that behaviourally in the default suite, which also makes the rule's claim that only desktop tests would catch it untrue.
findings.class_of: spellings of the gone codes the new text rules miss
findings.evidence: DirectoryReader.cs:152 `if (first && error == Kernel32.ERROR_FILE_NOT_FOUND)`. The spike folderdone-open-2-3-as-gone patch: `bool gone = !opened && count == 0 && (error == 2 || error == 3);`
findings.fix: Add a Scanner.cs pattern for a read error compared with the literals 2 or 3, for example `\berror\s*(?:==|is)\s*[23]\b` and `\bor\s+[23]\b(?![\w.])`. Reword the DirectoryReader rule's 'because' to name VanishedFolderTests as the real guard, or drop that rule as redundant with it.

dimensions_checked.result: M1. The must-verify '2/3 means gone' fails for a lost drive letter or a disconnected mapped share. Two web sources tie error 3 to disconnected mapped drives. Outside claim 9 (cloud and ProjFS placeholders) is recalled and only decorative: an opt-in CF test would show it. The cited rustfs PR #8479 does say what the design claims: NotFound from read_dir on a non-root child is treated as vanished, with a marker.

M1 (volume, letter or share loss). The 5 (delete pending) and 87 (replaced by a file) residues are left out on purpose, backed by the spikes' no-go and conditional verdicts; I accept that. In W-001 -Stopped they would still be OtherCodeDiffers (path gone, times unreadable, WindowCases.ps1:6661), so they make a run inconclusive, never failed. Rare; not raised. Root, links and the cancel path are checked and hold.

The stamp invariant holds by construction: there is a single call site (Scanner.cs:394-398, the only _unreadable.Add in src), and !opened implies count 0 because Read resets _count. The note's 'no notScanned: true' rule is also a single call site. The rule gaps are in m1.

none: the count, one note, one report key and the predicate are what the brief and its finish lines ask for. The DirectoryReader rule is weak and largely redundant with the behavioural test (m1), but cheap.
none: ScanResult.FoldersVanished (public init, set in Finish for every status) and core.foldersVanished (absent when core is null, schema 1 additive) are fully specified. The repro needs no new name.

Cancel during a vanished folder's open still gives 995, which returns Cancelled before the stamp (Scanner.cs:384). The missing root still ends RootUnreadable before FolderDone (Scanner.cs:200-205). The fix proposed for M1 must route its root re-open through io so Stop can cancel it on a dead share.
none: it matches the brief's prescribed fix (no flag, not in _unreadable, a new FoldersVanished count, a note like VanishedBeforeProbe, the row finishing as an empty folder).

m1. The new rules are already appended under '# settled by SL-005' (fitness.yaml:1510), so no ArchitectureRulesTests twin is needed. The note passes 'no count with a fixed plural' (it uses Count), 'only UnreadableRows writes a failed folder's kind' and 'the unread word is written once'. No new trait, so no FsaDefaultTestFilter clause.
M2: four material cases depend only on E007* tests that are not in the tree. The builder-owned tests cover none of the MainWindow or WindowReport lines, nor the code-3 row path.
none: the note is ASCII with no path, as Q-016 requires for the report. No new native calls, and nothing outside the cancel guard.
